starting_point.reported_exception: numpy._core._exceptions._UFuncBinaryResolutionError: ufunc 'subtract' cannot use operands with types dtype('O') and dtype('<m8[s]')

root_cause.summary: screening_framework.py already defined a `_naive_utc_ns(series)` helper specifically to convert a tz-aware datetime Series to a genuine `datetime64[ns]` numpy array (its own docstring explains exactly why: `Series.to_numpy()` on a tz-aware datetime column returns an `object` array of `Timestamp` instances, since numpy has no tz-aware datetime64 dtype -- object arrays cannot be subtracted from a `numpy.timedelta64`). However, this helper was never actually called anywhere in the module -- every function instead used a bare `pd.to_datetime(bars[time_col]).to_numpy()`, which silently produced an object-dtype array on this dataset's tz-aware `timestamp` column (confirmed: `data/historical_1m/task67a_development/*.csv`'s timestamp column parses to tz-aware UTC). The bug therefore was not a design flaw, only a call-site omission of an already-written fix.
root_cause.confirmed_by: grep for `_naive_utc_ns` usage in screening_framework.py returned exactly one hit (the function's own definition) before this fix.
affected_functions_pre_fix: causal_atr_proxy (line ~192: same pattern, this is the exact line/traceback reported)

sample_control_candidates (line ~479: `pool_times = pd.to_datetime(...).to_numpy()` then `.astype('datetime64[ns]').astype(np.int64)` -- this particular call chain happened not to raise the same UFuncTypeError since `.astype('datetime64[ns]')` on an object array of tz-aware Timestamps is accepted by numpy, but it silently drops the tz -- a correctness risk, not just a crash risk, so fixed for consistency even though it was not one of the 10 originally-failing tests -- its 2 failures were caused transitively via `add_bar_features` -> `causal_atr_proxy`)

fix.approach: Smallest robust fix: replaced every `pd.to_datetime(<tz-aware series>).to_numpy()` call site that feeds vectorized numpy datetime64 arithmetic with `_naive_utc_ns(<series>)`, which explicitly tz-converts to UTC then tz-localizes to None before calling `.to_numpy(dtype='datetime64[ns]')` -- guaranteeing a true datetime64 array, not object. No function signature changed; no caller-visible behavior changed for already-passing tests.
fix.deliberately_not_changed: add_trading_day's `trading_day` column was left tz-aware (NOT converted to naive) -- an earlier attempt to make it naive for consistency was reverted after discovering it would break sample_control_candidates's `session_start = day + day_open` / `eligible_start`/`eligible_end` scalar-Timestamp arithmetic against the (still tz-aware) bars['timestamp'] column, which would raise 'Cannot compare tz-naive and tz-aware timestamps'. `trading_day`'s only uses are equality comparisons (object-dtype Timestamp equality works fine) and scalar Timestamp arithmetic (also fine regardless of tz) -- neither hits the vectorized-subtraction bug, so leaving it tz-aware is correct and lower-risk than a broader tz-naive refactor.

additional_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_r.bug: Same-day warmup NOT correctly detected when a session's first bar has NO prior same-day bar within the window: searchsorted's `lo[i]` landed on the bar itself (index i), which trivially passed the `sym_days[lo[i]] == sym_days[i]` same-day check, producing a degenerate 1-bar 'window' (just the bar's own range) instead of the documented NaN-during-warmup behavior. Caught by test_causal_atr_proxy_same_day_only_and_warmup_nan (was masked by the dtype crash before this repair; started failing on its own once the dtype bug was fixed).
additional_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_r.fix: Added an explicit `if lo[i] >= i: continue` (equivalently `lo[i] == i`, since searchsorted guarantees lo[i] <= i) before the existing same-day check, requiring at least one genuine same-day bar strictly before position i within the window.

additional_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_r.bug: `pd.qcut(vol_pct[valid], q=3, labels=['LOW','MID','HIGH'], duplicates='drop')` raises ValueError('Bin labels must be one fewer than the number of bin edges') whenever vol_pct has enough ties that duplicates='drop' collapses to fewer than 3 actual bins (e.g. constant/near-constant volatility, which real DEVELOPMENT data won't have but small/synthetic fixtures can). Not a dtype bug; a fixed-length label list assumption. Surfaced test_sample_control_candidates_excludes_near_event_window and test_sample_control_candidates_respects_warmup_and_lead failing via add_bar_features.
additional_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_r.fix: Label count is now computed dynamically from the ACTUAL number of resulting bins (`bucketed.cat.categories.size`) rather than assumed to always be 3, sliced from ['LOW','MID','HIGH']; wrapped in try/except ValueError as a final fallback (leaves 'UNKNOWN' for that case, matching the module's existing insufficient-N philosophy).

additional_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_r.bug: Test used `assert row_60['bounded_by_session_close'] is True` -- an identity comparison. pandas always stores a bool-dtype DataFrame column as numpy bool dtype internally, so `.iloc[0]`/`[...]` scalar access on it always returns `numpy.bool_`, never the literal Python `True` singleton, regardless of what was originally inserted -- `numpy.bool_(True) is True` is False. This is a test-authoring bug, not a screening_framework.py defect (the underlying value was already correctly a bool via `bool(bounded_by_close)` in research_stats.forward_return_horizons).
additional_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_r.fix: Changed both assertions to `bool(row_N['bounded_by_session_close']) is True/False`, which correctly asserts the VALUE rather than relying on Python singleton identity through a pandas bool column.
